sources.note: Original indexed British Museum project page read; diagnostic/prognostic and therapeutic textual traditions, plant/mineral substances. Broad Mesopotamian/Babylonian framing, not claim of modern efficacy.

sources.title: Oracc, Old Babylonian Model Contracts
sources.note: Original indexed research introduction; school model contracts trained scribes on marriage, adoption, loans and land, but were not legally valid transactions.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Art of the Ancient Near East: Panel with Striding Lion
sources.note: Museum educator publication, printed object 23; approximately 120 glazed lions along Processional Way, New Year statues through Ishtar Gate.

sources.title: British Museum, The Cyrus Cylinder
sources.note: Direct original museum record indexed; 539 BCE conquest and Cyrus's building work, royal propaganda treated as a perspective rather than neutral chronicle.

proposedOverrides.summary: Babylonia’s cities, dynasties and temple culture persisted through conquest and renewal; this map shows only selected phases.

batchIdentityNotes: Exact imported babylonia record spans 1500 to 500 BCE, with polygon snapshots at 1500, 1000 and 700 BCE. This is incomplete map coverage, not one continuous independent polity; Hammurabi’s older kingdom and Cyrus’s 539 BCE conquest both fall outside or inside different edges. Public overview and ending explicitly distinguish these.
